updates.text: Markets: New York closes higher on Anthropic's prospectus; Meta and SpaceX raise money for AI; Brazilian listings fall
Geoecon: Tehran's joint statement promises more talks; Iran resubmits a seven-day plan for the straits

title: Four delegations met, and the inventories kept counting.

pages.title: Four delegations in Tehran, one pipeline in the desert

four-delegations-one-pipeline.title: Four delegations in Tehran, one pipeline in the desert
four-delegations-one-pipeline.dek: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey sat down with Iran's leaders on Monday. The Houthis said they hit the East-West pipeline again. Brent eased about 1.6%, which is what a meeting is worth before anything is signed.
four-delegations-one-pipeline.text: On Monday the defence minister of Saudi Arabia, Prince Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Turkey’s intelligence chief, Ibrahim Kalin, met Iran’s top security officials and negotiators in Tehran [1]. Iranian state television showed the Pakistani delegation sitting with President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [2]. Saudi Arabia’s deputy minister for public diplomacy, Rayed Krimly, called it part of the Makkah Defence Alliance’s efforts “for de-escalation”, in support of the mediation by Qatar and Pakistan [2]. It is the first high-level contact between Iran and all three members of that alliance since Saudi Arabia was drawn deeper into the conflict [2]. That is the news. The rest is a list of things that have not happened yet. What the room was for. Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman, Esmaeil Baqaei, said the “top priority” was the consequences of what Tehran calls the US-Israeli aggression [2]. AP reports that many Iranians are anxious about a return to all-out war, as Israeli and American leaders sharpen their threats before elections in both countries [1]. Four delegations in one room do not make a ceasefire. They do make a channel, and channels are dull, slow and the only thing that has ever ended a war. What the desert did. While the delegations met, the Houthis said they had struck pumping stations on Saudi Arabia’s East-West crude pipeline and Riyadh airport; Saudi Arabia did not immediately confirm damage [4]. The pipeline matters because it is the route around the straits: it carries Saudi crude to the Red Sea coast. It was shut for a time in September after drone attacks on pumping stations, then resumed [4]. Saudi Arabia said on Sunday it had intercepted more missiles and drones [3]. What the barrel said. Brent futures fell $1.90, or 1.63%, to $114.82 by 09:59 GMT, after a week in which Brent rose 6% [3]. CNBC had it at $115.86 by mid-morning New York time [5]. That is a modest discount for a meeting, on top of what one investment chief told CNBC is a risk premium of “about $20 a barrel” [5]. A PVM analyst put the trader’s view plainly: dips back to last week’s lows “will find grateful buyers” [3]. What the official series says. The EIA’s daily Brent spot price, the public-domain record, peaked at $135.51 on 2 October and stood at $115.22 on 20 October, its latest published value [6]. It lags the futures by several days, so read the chart as the shape of the autumn, not as today’s price. The shape is the point: the premium arrived in late September and has eased, not disappeared. The ledger view. Saudi Arabia also said on Monday it will start storing crude in Singapore from the second half of 2027 [5]. That is not a headline about war. It is a headline about inventory, which is what serious people do when they expect the next disruption to be ordinary. Storage contracts, pipeline repairs and insurance policies outlast speeches. So, usually, do the meetings that produce nothing on the first day. Nothing here is investment advice.

crude-in-singapore-from-2027.title: Crude in Singapore, from 2027
crude-in-singapore-from-2027.dek: Saudi Arabia will keep oil in storage near its Asian customers. It is the quietest strategic decision of the day.
crude-in-singapore-from-2027.text: Saudi Arabia will start storing crude oil in Singapore from the second half of 2027, energy ministers from both countries said on Monday, to shore up the resilience of supply in the region [1]. It is a modest sentence with a long logic behind it. The war that began at the end of February has disrupted shipping through both the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, and October has been the worst month for attacks on commercial shipping in those waters, according to data compiled by the Washington Institute for Near East Policy and cited by Reuters [2]. A barrel already sitting in Singapore does not need to pass a strait when a refinery calls. Storage is not glamorous. It costs money every month and earns nothing until the day it is needed. That is exactly why it is a better indicator of what producers expect than any statement: they are paying, in advance, for the next disruption to be survivable.

one-line-of-paper-and-a-seven-day-plan.title: One line of paper, and a seven-day plan
one-line-of-paper-and-a-seven-day-plan.dek: Tehran's four-way meeting ended with a joint statement. It promises more talking and names no date. Beside it, Iran put a staged plan for the straits back on the table, with conditions attached.
one-line-of-paper-and-a-seven-day-plan.text: This evening’s edition asked whether anything written would come out of Tehran. Something did. The joint statement calls Monday’s talks “the first meeting” of the four countries, and says the participants “agreed to continue the dialogue”, including for peace and security in the region [1]. Anadolu reports that the agenda covered regional security, Israel’s activities, and Palestine and Lebanon [2]. The published text names no date for a second round [1]. The more practical line came from beside the room. According to Iranian state outlets, Tehran has resubmitted, after technical talks in Doha, a plan to reopen shipping through the Strait of Hormuz in stages over seven days [3]. Its foreign ministry spokesman said Iranian negotiators were studying US counterproposals on lifting the naval blockade [3]. Tehran’s condition is that the seven days do not start until $24 billion in foreign reserves is fully accessible and container clearance at Bandar Abbas is freed [3]. A statement that promises more meetings is modest. A plan with a clock, a sum and a port in it is something a clerk can check. Watch for the second meeting’s date and for any reply on the sequence, not for adjectives. Nothing here is advice.

audi-builds-where-it-sells.title: Audi builds where it sells: $4 billion for Georgia
audi-builds-where-it-sells.dek: Volkswagen's premium brand plans its first US factory. Tariffs are argued about in speeches and answered in concrete.
audi-builds-where-it-sells.text: Audi plans to invest about $4 billion in its first US manufacturing plant, in Georgia, with around 4,500 jobs, according to Volkswagen [1]. Construction is due to start in 2027 and production in the early 2030s, with capacity for up to 200,000 premium SUVs a year for North American buyers [1]. Desk observation: a factory that opens in the 2030s is a bet on the market, not on any one administration. That is how trade policy is really answered.

podium-vs-print-continuing-and-88-8.title: Podium vs Print: "continuing" and 88.8
podium-vs-print-continuing-and-88-8.dek: The ifo president says the recovery is continuing. The ifo's own index of the current situation fell. Both are in the same release, and both are true.
podium-vs-print-continuing-and-88-8.text: “The recovery is continuing,” said Clemens Fuest, in the sentence every news agency used [2]. The ifo business climate rose for the sixth month in a row, to 90.2 points from 89.9, its highest since spring 2023, and above the 89.9 analysts had expected [1][2]. The print underneath. The climate is an average of two questions. Firms’ expectations for the next six months rose to 91.6 from 90.4. Their assessment of business right now fell to 88.8 from 89.5 [1]. The headline rose on hope; the present slipped. Where it is real. Manufacturing is the good news, and it is specific. Its balance turned positive, at +1.2, for the first time in more than three years; incoming orders rose and firms plan to expand production [1]. Services went the other way, to −1.2 from +0.7, with IT services the exception [1]. Trade was stuck at −17.2, construction improved to −15.5 [1]. The cautious reading. One bank analyst, Klaus Bauknecht of IKB, told tagesschau the survey shows no sign of a sustained investment upswing [2]. That is the right footnote. Orders are rising; capital spending is not yet in the numbers. The market. The DAX closed up 0.63% at 25,341.54; the CAC 40 fell 0.36% and Spain’s IBEX 0.73% [3]. Nothing here is investment advice.

ibex-and-psi-paid-for-brazil.title: Madrid and Lisbon paid for the Brazil result, Siemens Energy led the DAX
ibex-and-psi-paid-for-brazil.dek: Spanish and Portuguese shares, with large Brazilian exposure, slipped after the vote. The DAX's best performer was a turbine maker.
ibex-and-psi-paid-for-brazil.text: Dow Jones reported on Monday that Spanish and Portuguese shares were weighed down after the result in Brazil, where many of their listed companies earn money [1]. Spain’s IBEX 35 closed 0.73% lower at 18,850.30 [2]. In Frankfurt the story was different. By midday Siemens Energy had gained 3.9% and led the DAX, followed by Hochtief at 3.3%; Infineon rose 2.7% and Aixtron 2.9% as the AI-related names recovered [1]. The DAX closed 0.63% higher at 25,341.54 [2]. The pairing says something useful. Markets react to elections in hours, and to order books over months. A turbine maker’s gain is about contracts already signed; a bank’s loss on Brazil is about a complaint not yet heard. Nothing here is investment advice.

a-prospectus-and-the-bill-for-the-buildi.title: A prospectus, and the bill for the buildings
a-prospectus-and-the-bill-for-the-buildi.dek: New York closed higher on an AI company's filing. The more useful numbers sat beside it: who is borrowing for the chips, and what Brazilian listings paid for Sunday.
a-prospectus-and-the-bill-for-the-buildi.text: New York finished Monday higher. The S&P 500 rose 0.7% to 7,676.77 and the Nasdaq Composite 0.82% to 26,169.38, after Anthropic published its prospectus for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker “ANT” [1]. The filing shows $16.29 billion of revenue for the six months to June, against $1.16 billion a year earlier [1]. The invoices beside it. Meta said it plans to raise $95 billion for its AI investments, and Elon Musk said SpaceX has closed $40 billion of debt for AI chips [1]. Chipmakers rallied, yet the iShares semiconductor fund is still roughly 25% below its high [1]. Brent settled 0.8% lower at $115.81 a barrel [1]. The other side of the board. US-listed Brazilian shares paid for Sunday’s result. Petrobras fell 21% before the open, and the iShares MSCI Brazil fund dropped nearly 20% overnight before paring the loss to 18% [1]. This evening’s edition asked who pays for the buildings. Tonight’s partial answer: new shareholders and lenders, in sums now written down. Futures put the chance of the Fed holding at 3.75–4% on Wednesday at about 90%, the same evening Alphabet and Microsoft report [1]. That is where the bills get read. Nothing here is investment advice.

the-ten-year-sits-at-five.title: The ten-year sits at five, France slips under it
the-ten-year-sits-at-five.dek: The US benchmark yield hovered around 5% on Monday. The French ten-year fell below 5% after Moody's.
the-ten-year-sits-at-five.text: The US ten-year Treasury yield edged up to 5% by Monday midday, Dow Jones reported, while the French ten-year fell below 5% after Moody’s held the country’s rating [1]. The official H.15 series shows 4.96% for Thursday, 22 October, its latest value [2]. For once, Paris borrowed for ten years at about the same price as Washington. That is less a compliment to either than a reminder of what a decade of debt costs everyone. Nothing here is investment advice.

the-count-holds-the-complaint-files.title: Brazil: the count holds, the complaint gets filed
the-count-holds-the-complaint-files.dek: Lula won with 51.79%. Flávio Bolsonaro wants the vote annulled over a two-hour extension both campaigns had asked for in some form. The institutions now do the slow part.
the-count-holds-the-complaint-files.text: Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court has Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva at 51.79% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 48.21%, a margin of about 4.4 million votes [3]. AP reports Lula persuaded some 10 million additional voters between the rounds, and is due to take office for a fourth, non-consecutive term on 5 January 2027 [1]. The complaint. Bolsonaro said what happened on Sunday “was not normal” and called for the result to be annulled [2]. His objection is a decision by Supreme Court justice Cristiano Zanin to extend voting nationwide by two hours [2]. Lula’s campaign had asked for the extension, citing voter transport problems; Bolsonaro’s campaign had asked for extra time too, but only in municipalities in five states hit by rain, floods and power cuts [2]. The rest of the world. The EU, Mexico, Canada and Russia sent congratulations; Canada’s Mark Carney wrote of “new promising commercial prospects” [4]. Donald Trump and Argentina’s Javier Milei had not publicly reacted by Monday, BBC Brasil reported [5]; Donald Trump Jr criticised the extension [4]. The sequence is the familiar one: a count, a complaint, a court. Brazil has run it before: Jair Bolsonaro also refused to concede in 2022 [2]. The dull machinery usually wins when it is allowed to finish.

one-vote-two-ballots-no-deal.title: Electoral reform: a year late, and 23 winners outside
one-vote-two-ballots-no-deal.dek: The coalition promised that every constituency winner gets a seat without the Bundestag growing again. Its working group has not found how.
one-vote-two-ballots-no-deal.text: Germany’s coalition agreed to change the electoral law so that every candidate who wins a constituency also gets a seat, while keeping the Bundestag at 630 members, down from 736 [1]. So far, the coalition’s working group has found no alternative to the system introduced under the previous government, tagesschau reports, and Chancellor Friedrich Merz says the coalition is a year behind [1]. The stakes are concrete. After the last federal election, 23 constituency winners could not take their seats, most of them from the CDU and CSU [1]. The CSU and the Left, unusually, agree on the complaint [1]. The deadline is administrative, which is why it is real. Constituency boundaries have to be redrawn, with the Länder involved, before the next election, and that takes time, as Merz put it: “Das ist ein aufwändiger Prozess” [1]. Electoral law is the most boring law a democracy has. It is also the one everybody else depends on.

who-congratulated-and-who-waited.title: Who congratulated, and who waited
who-congratulated-and-who-waited.dek: Brussels, Mexico City, Ottawa and Moscow sent messages. Washington and Buenos Aires had not by Monday.
who-congratulated-and-who-waited.text: Ursula von der Leyen called Lula’s win a victory for “democracy and multilateralism”, and António Costa congratulated him for the European Council [1]. Vladimir Putin sent a message through the Kremlin [1]; Mexico’s Claudia Sheinbaum and Canada’s Mark Carney posted their congratulations [2]. Donald Trump and Javier Milei had not reacted publicly by Monday, BBC Brasil reported [1]. Recognition is a diplomatic form, not a legal one: Brazil’s courts, not foreign capitals, settle the complaint.

the-mood-is-a-cost-of-living-line.title: Stress has a line item, and it is the cost of living
the-mood-is-a-cost-of-living-line.dek: In the APA's annual survey, 77% of US adults name the cost of living as a significant source of stress. The economy is second, money third. Worry has become an accounting category.
the-mood-is-a-cost-of-living-line.text: The American Psychological Association’s Stress in America report for 2026 found that 77% of US adults call the cost of living a significant source of stress, 74% the economy and 71% money [1]. The survey covered 3,132 adults online between 29 July and 24 August 2026 [1]. A health-policy commentator read it on Monday as stress becoming “the new normal” [2]. The reading. The three top answers are one answer in three coats. They are about prices, and they come from a year of war-priced oil. The report’s title is about uncertainty, which is the right word: the bill you cannot predict is heavier than the bill you can. The European contrast. Monday’s ifo survey shows German firms more hopeful about the next six months than about today: expectations at 91.6, the current situation at 88.8 [3]. Firms can see their order books. Households mostly see the receipt. Those two moods meet, eventually, in payrolls. A survey is not a diagnosis. It is, though, a useful reminder that the remedy for worry about prices is rarely a speech. It is a predictable bill.

hope-ran-ahead-of-the-order-book.title: Hope ran 2.8 points ahead of today
hope-ran-ahead-of-the-order-book.dek: German firms' expectations rose to 91.6, their view of the present fell to 88.8. That gap is a mood, not yet a fact.
hope-ran-ahead-of-the-order-book.text: The ifo survey asks about 9,000 firms two questions: how is business now, and how will it be over the next six months [1]. In October the answers moved apart. The expectations index rose to 91.6 from 90.4; the current situation fell to 88.8 from 89.5 [1]. Desk arithmetic: expectations now stand 2.8 points above the present. In April the order was reversed, with expectations at 83.9 below a situation of 85.4 [1]. Firms were then gloomier about the future than about the present; now they are more hopeful. Psychologically that is the healthier gap. It is also the one that has to be paid for: if orders keep arriving, the present catches up; if they do not, expectations fall back to meet it. Manufacturing, where incoming orders rose, is where the hope has the best collateral [1].

a-pipeline-a-reserve-and-a-tank-in-singa.title: A pipeline claim, a reserve release and a tank in Singapore
a-pipeline-a-reserve-and-a-tank-in-singa.dek: The Houthis say they hit East-West pumping stations; Riyadh has not confirmed damage. Washington lent 400,000 barrels to one refinery. Saudi Arabia will store crude in Singapore from 2027. German power is back at €116.57.
a-pipeline-a-reserve-and-a-tank-in-singa.text: The Houthis said on Monday they attacked pumping stations on Saudi Arabia’s East-West crude pipeline and Riyadh airport [1]. Saudi Arabia did not immediately confirm the attacks or any damage [1]. The pipeline, which takes crude from the Gulf side to the Red Sea, was shut for a time in September after drone strikes on pumping stations and then resumed [1]. The reserve. In the US, the Energy Department said on Friday it had authorised a release of 400,000 barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, to cover a supply disruption at a Louisiana refinery [2]. That is a small, targeted loan, which is exactly what a reserve is for. The tank. Saudi Arabia will start storing crude oil in Singapore from the second half of 2027, the two countries’ energy ministers said on Monday, to make supply in the region more resilient [2]. Inventory near the customer is the oldest insurance in the trade. The socket. In Germany, the day-ahead power price averaged €116.57 per megawatt hour for delivery on Monday, after €13.12 on storm-blown Sunday and €30.12 on Saturday [3]. The wind fell; the price remembered gas. Nothing here is advice.

above-120-the-demand-answers.title: Above $120, the customer answers
above-120-the-demand-answers.dek: One investment chief puts the war premium at about $20 a barrel, and sees demand giving way if Brent goes past $120. The longer worry is refineries.
above-120-the-demand-answers.text: Michael Alfaro, chief investment officer at Gallo Partners, told CNBC on Monday that the risk premium in oil is “about $20 a barrel” [1]. A substantial strike on Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline or on refining infrastructure could send prices sharply higher, he said, but further gains would eventually weaken consumption, with more demand destruction setting in above $120 a barrel for Brent [1]. The more durable point in the same report is about refining. Damage to refineries could become a longer structural problem, extending into 2027 and beyond [1]. Crude can be rerouted; a refinery cannot be rebuilt in a month. Prices are a conversation between producers and buyers. When buyers start driving less, heating less and ordering later, they are answering. That is not a forecast, just how invoices behave. Nothing here is investment advice.

sunday-wind-monday-price.title: Sunday's wind, Monday's price
sunday-wind-monday-price.dek: Onshore turbines delivered more than 1,000 GWh on each storm day. Monday's day-ahead price was nine times Sunday's.
sunday-wind-monday-price.text: German onshore wind generated 1,009,162 MWh on Saturday and 1,019,966 MWh on Sunday, against 242,281 MWh last Wednesday, according to SMARD [1]. The day-ahead price followed: €30.12 on Saturday, €13.12 on Sunday and €116.57 for Monday [1]. Desk arithmetic: Monday’s average is almost nine times Sunday’s. Wind is cheap when it blows and silent about tomorrow, which is why the grid still keeps everything else on standby.

two-committees-two-days-apart.title: Two committees, two days apart, and France gets a quieter week
two-committees-two-days-apart.dek: The Fed meets on Tuesday and Wednesday, the ECB decides on Thursday. Both have held since September. Moody's kept France at Aa3, and the French ten-year slipped below 5%.
two-committees-two-days-apart.text: The Federal Reserve’s committee meets on 27 and 28 October [1]. The ECB’s Governing Council announces its decision on Thursday, 29 October. Both arrive on hold: the Fed’s upper limit has been 4.00% since September, the ECB’s deposit rate 2.50% since September [2]. The expectation. Previews broadly expect the ECB to hold at 2.50%; one market-pricing tracker put the chance of an October rise at about 3%, and Morgan Stanley sees December, when new staff projections arrive, as the “natural moment” for the next move [3]. A forecast is not a decision. The chart shows only what was decided. The relief. Moody’s has kept France at Aa3, citing a diversified economy and strong public institutions despite rising debt and a fragmented parliament [4]. The French ten-year yield fell below 5% on Monday morning [4]. That is the most useful thing a rating agency can say about a country: the institutions still count. Nothing here is investment advice.

december-is-the-natural-moment.title: Thursday is for holding, December for deciding
december-is-the-natural-moment.dek: Previews expect the ECB to leave the deposit rate at 2.50%. The argument is about the sentence after.
december-is-the-natural-moment.text: The ECB raised its deposit rate by a quarter point in September, to 2.50%, and previews now broadly expect it to hold on Thursday [1]. Market pricing gives an October rise only a small chance; Morgan Stanley calls December, when the staff publish new projections, the “natural moment” for any next step [1]. ING argues that rising bond yields favour a hold, because they already tighten financing conditions [2]. That last point is the one to keep. A central bank does not only set one rate; it watches the rates everyone else charges. When long yields rise by themselves, part of the committee’s work is done for it. So the decision itself is likely the least informative part of Thursday. The sentences after it, about energy, wages and those yields, are where the next move will be written. Nothing here is investment advice.

ordinary-ledger-the-afternoon-price.title: Ordinary Ledger: the afternoon price is €174.58
ordinary-ledger-the-afternoon-price.dek: Heating oil edged up 24 cents per 100 litres between Monday morning and afternoon on the German average, although Brent fell. The exchange reaches the tank a day late.
ordinary-ledger-the-afternoon-price.text: The German average for 100 litres of heating oil stood at €174.58 on Monday afternoon, for a standard order, according to HeizOel24 [1]. That is €3.94 more than a week ago and €41.03 more than three months ago [1]. This morning the same page showed €174.34. Brent, meanwhile, fell more than 1.5% during the day [2]. The ledger. Desk arithmetic: a 3,000-litre delivery at the afternoon average costs about €5,237, roughly €7 more than at breakfast and about €1,231 more than three months ago. A detached house uses 2,000 to 3,000 litres a year, by the portal’s rule of thumb [1]. The lag. A cheaper barrel does not make a cheaper tank on the same day. Taxes, the CO₂ levy, the dollar and dealers’ margins sit between them, and the portal itself rates the moment to buy as “ungünstig”, unfavourable [1]. An order is binding, and the price holds until delivery in two to four weeks [1]. Nothing here is advice.

two-to-three-thousand-litres.title: Two to three thousand litres, and 15 per square metre
two-to-three-thousand-litres.dek: The heating oil portal's own rules of thumb turn a price per 100 litres into a winter.
two-to-three-thousand-litres.text: HeizOel24 says a detached house uses about 2,000 to 3,000 litres of heating oil a year, about 15 litres per square metre, with 10 to 20% of it going on hot water [1]. Desk arithmetic at Monday afternoon’s average of €174.58 per 100 litres: 2,000 litres cost about €3,492 and 3,000 litres about €5,237. Your own meter reading beats any rule of thumb. Nothing here is advice.

three-invoices-due-on-wednesday-and-thur.title: Alphabet and Microsoft on Wednesday, Amazon and Intel on Thursday
three-invoices-due-on-wednesday-and-thur.dek: About 160 S&P 500 companies report this week. The question for the hyperscalers is not whether AI demand exists. It is who pays for the buildings.
three-invoices-due-on-wednesday-and-thur.text: Alphabet and Microsoft report after the US close on Wednesday; Amazon and Intel after the close on Thursday [1]. Around 160 S&P 500 companies report this week, and about 83% of those that reported by Friday beat earnings expectations, according to FactSet data cited by CNBC [1]. The receipt that came first. Meta reported last week: revenue up 26%, but capital spending of $34.91 billion in the quarter turned free cash flow negative, and the shares fell nearly 7% [2]. That is the template for this week. The demand is real; the question is the bill. What analysts are watching. For Alphabet, revenue growth of about 25% is expected, after last quarter’s raised capex forecast in a “supply-constrained environment” [1]. For Microsoft, Azure’s pace [1]. For Intel, analysts expect revenue growth of about 20.5% [1]. At home. In Monday’s ifo survey, German IT service providers were the bright spot of an otherwise weaker services sector [3]. Data centres need electricians and invoices as well as chips. Nothing here is investment advice.

demand-ahead-of-supply.title: "Demand continues to run ahead of supply"
demand-ahead-of-supply.dek: Intel reports on Thursday. The line analysts keep quoting is about shortage, not hype.
demand-ahead-of-supply.text: Intel reports after the US close on Thursday, alongside Amazon [1]. Last quarter it posted its highest quarterly revenue growth since 2011; this time analysts expect revenue up about 20.5% and earnings per share up about 70% on the year, according to LSEG data cited by CNBC [1]. UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri noted that Intel said “demand continues to run ahead of supply” [1]. That is the most interesting sentence of the AI season, because it is about factories, not models. Shortage is a physical fact. It shows up in delivery times and prices, and it is resolved by capacity, which takes years. For Amazon, Jefferies says AWS “is not yet done accelerating” [1]. Both claims will meet their invoices on Thursday evening. Nothing here is investment advice.

ebola-88-cases-38-deaths-1008-in-care.title: Ebola: 88 cases, 38 deaths, and 958 patients for 1,583 beds
ebola-88-cases-38-deaths-1008-in-care.dek: The 24 October bulletin puts the Bundibugyo outbreak at 9,964 confirmed cases. The daily average is rising again. Nord-Kivu is over capacity.
ebola-88-cases-38-deaths-1008-in-care.text: The Congolese bulletin for 24 October reports 88 new confirmed cases and 38 deaths, taking the outbreak to 9,964 confirmed cases and 4,841 deaths, a case fatality rate of 48.6% [1]. Over the past seven days the average was 72.7 cases and 40.0 deaths a day, against 68.1 and 32.1 the week before [1]. Where. Ituri reported 44 of the new cases, Nord-Kivu 39 and Haut-Uélé 5 [1]. No new health zone has been affected since 16 October; the outbreak stays in 66 zones across eight provinces [1]. WHO’s latest update also lists imported cases in Kenya and Nigeria [2]. The machinery. Treatment centres hold 958 patients for 1,583 beds, but Nord-Kivu has 495 patients for 410 beds [1]. Teams saw 87.1% of contacts; 9,415 people have been vaccinated since 26 August [1]. Of 38 deaths, 26 happened outside a treatment centre [1], which is where the next infections usually start. The good line, small but real: 2,670 people have recovered [1].

nubeqa-58-per-cent.title: A trial result worth reading slowly: 58%
nubeqa-58-per-cent.dek: Bayer reports that adding its prostate cancer drug to standard treatment cut the risk of metastasis or death by 58% in an interim analysis.
nubeqa-58-per-cent.text: Bayer said an interim analysis of the Phase III DASL-HiCaP trial showed a statistically significant 58% reduction in the risk of metastasis or death when darolutamide (NUBEQA) was added to hormone therapy and radiation, compared with placebo [1]. Interim means the trial continues and the full data will follow. A relative reduction is not a promise for any one patient; the number that matters to you is the one your doctor reads from the full paper.

lilly-on-thursday.title: Thursday's other invoice: Eli Lilly
lilly-on-thursday.dek: The GLP-1 maker reports before the bell. Analysts expect revenue up more than 28%.
lilly-on-thursday.text: Eli Lilly reports before the US open on Thursday; LSEG data cited by CNBC expects revenue growth of more than 28% on the year [1]. Goldman Sachs says investors will watch for a raised full-year outlook as Mounjaro and Zepbound “continue to shine” [1]. Medicines for weight and diabetes have become one of the largest businesses in health care. The question for health systems is not the share price but the reimbursement bill behind it.

seventy-drones-over-voronezh-talks-in-no.title: Seventy drones over Voronezh, talks pencilled in for November
seventy-drones-over-voronezh-talks-in-no.dek: Russia launched 140 drones and four missiles at Ukraine overnight; Ukraine's drones hit Voronezh. Both sides have agreed to meet again, with the US, next month.
seventy-drones-over-voronezh-talks-in-no.text: Russia launched 140 drones and four missiles at Ukraine overnight; Ukraine’s air force said 112 drones and three Kh-59/69 missiles were shot down [1]. Strikes injured people in Zaporizhzhia, Chernihiv and Izium, and damage to an energy facility forced emergency power cuts in the Khmelnytskyi region [1]. The other direction. In Russia, the Voronezh governor said more than 70 drones were shot down over the city; two people were killed and 17 injured, many on a commuter train hit by debris [1]. The paper track. Russia agreed last Wednesday to return to three-way talks with Ukraine and the US in November, in Abu Dhabi according to Moscow [1]. President Zelenskyy said on Sunday: “We are ready to talk,” adding that territory must be settled at leaders’ level [1]. On Friday, the two sides agreed a localised ceasefire around Oleshky in Kherson [1]. A ceasefire around one town is small. Small agreements are the ones that get kept, and kept agreements are the ones that get copied.

october-the-worst-month-at-sea.title: October, the worst month at sea
october-the-worst-month-at-sea.dek: Attacks on commercial shipping around Hormuz and nearby waters peaked this month, by one think tank's count.
october-the-worst-month-at-sea.text: October has been the worst month for attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waterways, according to data compiled by the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, which has tracked maritime security incidents since 2017, Reuters reports [1]. The Houthis also said they had struck Riyadh airport over the weekend; Saudi Arabia said on Sunday it intercepted more missiles and drones [1]. Navies and insurers keep the count; the count is what sets the premium.

the-rhine-at-55-centimetres.title: The Rhine at Kaub reads 55 centimetres, and the next front is on its way
the-rhine-at-55-centimetres.dek: A day after it cleared its 2018 low, the Kaub gauge has climbed by more than 20 centimetres. Storm Manja's remnants left, the warm front of NAOMI arrives in the north-west tonight.
the-rhine-at-55-centimetres.text: The Rhine gauge at Kaub read 55 cm at 16:30 on Monday, according to the federal waterways’ PEGELONLINE service [1]. Desk arithmetic on the 15-minute readings: the mean so far today is about 53 cm, against 31.3 cm on Sunday and 24.5 cm on Saturday [1]. The service still classes the level as low against the long-term mean low water [1]. The weather behind it. The German Weather Service said on Monday morning that the remains of storm Manja were moving off over the Norwegian Sea, with gusts of around 70 km/h on the North Sea coast and up to 95 km/h on exposed summits such as the Brocken [2]. On Monday evening the warm front of the next storm, NAOMI, west of Ireland, reaches the north-west half of the country [2]. Why it matters. Kaub is the bottleneck gauge for Rhine shipping between the Upper and Middle Rhine. Every centimetre there is cargo a barge can carry instead of leaving at the quay. Rain upstream is, for once, a supply-chain story with a happy direction.

ninety-five-on-the-brocken.title: Ninety-five on the Brocken, and a turn to the south
ninety-five-on-the-brocken.dek: The DWD's Monday warning: storm gusts at the coast and on the summits, easing, then a fresh front from the west.
ninety-five-on-the-brocken.text: The German Weather Service forecast gusts of around 70 km/h on the North Sea coast on Monday, up to 85 km/h on the North Frisian Islands at first, and 80 to 95 km/h on exposed summits such as the Brocken and the Fichtelberg, easing through the day [1]. Overnight into Tuesday the wind on the North Sea picks up again and turns south, with gusts of 60 to 70 km/h, as the warm front of storm NAOMI arrives [1]. Two storms in a week: good for the turbines, a test for the roof tiles.

rain-floods-and-the-ballot.title: Rain, floods and the ballot box
rain-floods-and-the-ballot.dek: One reason Brazil's voting hours became a legal fight: heavy rain and power cuts in five states.
rain-floods-and-the-ballot.text: Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign had asked for longer voting hours in municipalities across five states, citing heavy rain, flooding and power outages, DW reports; Lula’s campaign asked for a nationwide extension over voter transport problems, and the court granted that [1]. Weather does not take sides. It does test whether polling stations, roads and power lines can carry an election, and that is an infrastructure question long before it is a legal one.

rates-fed-ecb-26pm.title: Two committees, two days apart, both on hold since September

rates-fed-ecb-26pm.alt: Step chart since January 2025 of the Fed funds target upper limit and the ECB deposit rate. The Fed's upper limit falls from 4.50% to 3.75% between September and December 2025, then rises to 4.00% in September 2026. The ECB deposit rate falls from 3.00% to 2.00% by June 2025, rises to 2.25% in June 2026 and to 2.50% in September 2026. Both are unchanged since September; the latest values, for 26 October 2026, are 4.00% and 2.50%. The Fed meets on 27–28 October and the ECB decides on 29 October.
